Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard from you:
- Primary workload: real-time customer support generation + document summarization for billing disputes.
- Volume: ~50k requests/day, average prompt+response ~750 tokens, peak concurrency ~120 RPS during billing cycle spikes.
- Key evaluation criteria: latency (95th pct < 300ms), cost per 1M tokens, and predictable SLA for peak periods.

Redwood differentiators we highlighted:
- Production-first runtime with KV prefix caching and workload-aware batching to reduce per-token cost.
- Dedicated routing for predictable performance during spikes and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants.
- Transparent unit economics and a recommended starter TCO calculation (attached).

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to run a short cost/TCO plan comparing Redwood vs your hyperscaler run (we'll use your token profile and assumptions).
2) We set up a 48-hour sandbox test next week: 1M tokens baseline, with and without caching; we'll surface batch sizes and latency percentiles.
3) Hand over SI contact for procurement questions (Laura) — she can help with the SOW/contract timeline.

Attaching: Redwood_TCO_1M_tokens.xlsx with base assumptions and a couple of cost scenarios.

Is next Wednesday (7/22) for the 48-hour sandbox still good?

Thanks Samira — answering inline and adding Marcus (SE) and Lauren (Legal/Procurement ops):

> 1) Can you confirm the assumptions you used in the attached workbook for per-1M token cost? Specifically: batching assumptions, cache hit rate, and model variants.

Yes — quick summary of the assumptions in the attached workbook (and I'll paste the short table below):
- Model: opensource Llama-3-7B optimized; hyperscaler baseline uses comparable 7B family.
- Batching: Redwood baseline uses dynamic batching with average batch size 12 for this workload (you'll see a sensitivity column for batch sizes 1/6/12/24).
- Cache: we assumed a 28% prefix/KV cache hit rate for the summary flows; we included scenarios for 0%, 28%, and 55% cache hits.
- Per-1M tokens: Redwood (baseline, caching 28%, batch 12) = $45.2 per 1M tokens. Hyperscaler (on-demand GPUs, similar model family, no custom prefix cache) = $82.6 per 1M tokens.

> 2) For the sandbox, can you include an apples-to-apples cost line item that factors in instance overhead and spot vs on-demand?

Yes — Marcus will prepare a TCO comparison that includes instance amortization, networking, and NVMe costs and will show both spot and on-demand-equivalent numbers. Marcus — can you pull a spot/on-demand delta for a 4xA10-like configuration and include how Redwood amortizes multi-tenant serving overhead vs dedicated pools?

> 3) Procurement will need SOC2 + encryption at rest statement — looped Lauren for procurement/contract cadence. Lauren — can you confirm the SOC2 & encryption statement + an initial SOW cadence (we typically provide a 2-week sandbox SOW)?

Thanks — I'll schedule the sandbox for Wed 7/22 1:00pm PST unless you prefer morning.

Aditya

Hi Samira, Aditya —

I pulled together the short TCO notes and attached a PDF (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-costs.pdf). Key highlights (apples-to-apples basis):

Assumptions: 1M tokens = average request/response sizes per your profile (~750 tokens total). 95th pct latency target = 300ms.

Redwood baseline (multi-tenant serving, dynamic batching, 28% cache hit):
- Per-1M tokens: $45.2
- Typical 95th latency (sandbox sim): 220–280ms depending on batch window
- Notes: cache effective reduces tokenized compute by ~20–30% for summary-heavy flows

Hyperscaler baseline (on-demand GPU endpoints, no prefix caching, similar model family):
- Per-1M tokens: $82.6 (on-demand)
- Spot-mode alt: $60.4 per 1M tokens (but with preemption risk and additional engineering complexity for fallbacks)

Breakdown callouts (included in PDF):
- Batch size sensitivity: batch=1 -> +60% cost; batch=24 -> -18% cost vs baseline batch=12.
- Cache hit sensitivity: 0% -> +38% cost; 55% -> -26% cost.
- Network/storage/ops overhead: hyperscaler endpoints show higher instance-level overhead in our benchmarking because per-request cold starts/owner allocation is less efficient for bursty traffic.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-costs.pdf (short deck) and I uploaded a 12-min demo recording to the linked Drive.

Next tests I propose for the 48-hour sandbox:
1) Baseline 1M tokens run with no cache (to validate raw compute cost).
2) 1M tokens run with simulated 30% and 55% cache hit rates to measure effective token reduction and latency delta.
3) Stress test for peak concurrency (120–150 RPS) to validate 95th pct latency under burst.

Samira — if you can share an S3 token log sample or similar trace we can use to seed the cache simulation that would make the sandbox results more representative.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
